script.question: A person receives **₹2,200 at the start of each year** for 2 years. Interest is 10% p.a. compounded annually. What is the **present value** of this annuity?

lines.say: A person gets ₹2,200 at the start of each year for 2 years, at 10% compound interest. What is the present value?
Most students discount both payments, 2,200 divided by 1.1, plus 2,200 divided by 1.21. That gives ₹3,818.18. Right?
The right answer is ₹4,200. Here's why.
Step one. The payments are at the start of each year.
So the first ₹2,200 comes today. Today means no discounting.
Step two. The second payment comes after 1 year only.
Discount it once at 10%. Divide by 1.1.
Step three. Add the two values.
The ₹3,818.18 is correct only for payments at the end of each year.
The shortcut. Annuity due equals ordinary annuity multiplied by 1 plus i. Here 3,818.18 × 1.1 gives ₹4,200. Or take the first payment, plus an ordinary annuity for one year less.
Your turn. A person receives ₹3,300 at the start of each year for 2 years, at 10% p.a. Find the present value. Write your answer in the comments.
Comment your answer. Follow for a QT trap every day.

check_notes: "Your turn." is said twice in a row.
The card "2,200 + 2,000 = ₹4,200" appears while the spoken line is about ₹3,818.18 being correct only for end-of-year payments, so speech and card don't match.
"Most students fall for it" is an unsupported claim.
